clue.text: Having done half a U-turn getting to the correct viewpoints

parts.note: 'at' and 'to' both mark a place you arrive at
the correct one is the right one
angles are points of view, as in looking at a story from a new angle

explanation.surface: Someone turning partway round finds a better view of things.
explanation.walkthrough: A U-turn is 180 degrees, so half of one is a 90-degree turn. 'getting' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Half a U-turn is a quarter turn of ninety degrees, leaving you perpendicular to where you faced.

clue.text: Generally a sign of error by the committee

parts.note: a cross is the mark a teacher makes for a wrong answer
taken as written
a board is a committee, as a board of directors

explanation.surface: A committee's mistake becomes evident throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying to everyone alike, in all cases, is to apply generally.

clue.text: Regarded as part of elaborate deception

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something seen as part of an intricate trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rated is to be considered or judged in some way.

clue.text: Young composer, not yet developed

parts.note: green means young and inexperienced
John Field was an Irish composer, inventor of the nocturne

explanation.surface: A youthful composer whose talent has not matured.
explanation.walkthrough: A greenfield site is land never built on, used in British planning talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenfield site is undeveloped countryside, not previously built upon.

clue.text: Appallingly wet day hides island in the Channel

indicators.note: hides says the jumble keeps the letter for island concealed within it
appallingly signals that wet day is badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A dreadful rainy day conceals an island in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' puts I inside TDEWAY, an anagram of WET DAY. 'in the' is a link; 'Channel' is not the English one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tideway is a channel in which a tide flows, or the tidal stretch of a river.

clue.text: Issues a book

explanation.surface: A single book's matters of concern.
explanation.walkthrough: Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Issues of a magazine are its successive editions; the Bible's fourth book of Moses carries the name too.

clue.text: Weak fabric

explanation.surface: A flimsy piece of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble excuse is unconvincing; lamé is a fabric woven with metallic threads.

clue.text: Sailor preferred over soldiers to make explosive

indicators.note: in a down entry over puts the sailor's word above the rest

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor
a pet is a favourite, the one preferred
RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

explanation.surface: A seaman favoured over the army for making bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link; saltpetre (potassium nitrate) is the key ingredient of gunpowder.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate is the oxidising ingredient of gunpowder, a substance used for blasting.

clue.text: Half the crew made outstanding deal on tour of duty

parts.note: a star performer is outstanding
deal is pine or fir wood, a plank or board of it
a watch is a sailor's turn on duty

explanation.surface: Half a ship's company strike a great bargain during their service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' and 'on' are links. A ship's crew is split into the port and starboard watches, on duty by turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company is divided into two watches, one named for the right-hand side of the vessel.

clue.text: Crazy turn after heel to port

indicators.note: after puts the flipped word behind the word for heel

parts.note: a heel is a cad, a rotter

indicators.note: turn tells us the word for crazy is flipped round to read backwards

parts.note: crazy means mad

explanation.surface: A mad change of course after tilting the ship over to the left-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' and 'port' pretend to be sailing terms (a ship heeling, the port side); 'heel' is a scoundrel and 'port' is the Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major Dutch seaport, one of the busiest harbours in Europe.

clue.text: A fine swindle

explanation.surface: A penalty imposed for cheating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a monetary penalty; as a verb it means to cheat someone out of money.

clue.text: A battle for the chair, perhaps

explanation.surface: Rivals fight over who gets to sit in the chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Sedan was an 1870 battle of the Franco-Prussian War; a sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles.
explanation.definitionFit: The French town gave its name to an 1870 battle, and a carried seat for one passenger shares the name.

clue.text: What women must do while men work?

definitions.text: What women must do while men work?

parts.words: What women must do while men work?
parts.note: recalls Charles Kingsley's line from The Three Fishers: men must work and women must cry

explanation.surface: A question about the division of labour between the sexes.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue quotes Kingsley's poem The Three Fishers, where the wives on shore shed tears while the fishermen go to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kingsley's poem the fishermen's wives are left to shed tears as the men go out to sea.

clue.text: Succeeded with the standard argument

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
par is the standard or norm, as in up to par

explanation.surface: Someone wins a debate by sticking to accepted norms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to quarrel or dispute, and a spar is a squabble or wrangle.

clue.text: In Paris, very dated tourist centre for the unwelcome visitor

parts.note: tres is French for very
passe means out of date

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the word tourist

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned tourist hub in Paris attracts people who are not wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone entering property without permission is an intruder, a visitor not welcomed.

clue.text: Sample popular drink inside the House, perhaps

indicators.note: inside places the words for popular and drink within the word for sample

parts.note: to sample is to try
in means fashionable or popular
It is Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Tasting a fashionable cocktail in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Trinity House is the body that runs Britain's lighthouses, so 'the House, perhaps' defines Trinity by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity House is the authority for lighthouses and pilots in England and Wales, so it may be called just 'the House'.

clue.text: Very soon desert a lover

parts.note: in a mo is British slang for in a moment, very soon
to rat is to desert or betray

explanation.surface: A partner is about to abandon their beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mo' is British colloquial for in a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a sweetheart.

clue.text: Totters out, going faster than before

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of totters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone staggers off, picking up speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Stretto is a musical direction: a passage played faster, especially at the close.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a stretto passage quickens its tempo, often toward the end of a piece.

clue.text: Female bishop was first to be authorized

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name, standing for a female
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to have been first is to have led

explanation.surface: A woman bishop was the first to be given permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' gives a woman's name, ENA, a crossword favourite. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enabled is to be given the power or permission to do something.

clue.text: Intend to have time in New York to eat outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for eat goes around the time zone letters

parts.note: to dine is to eat
EST is Eastern Standard Time, the time zone of New York

explanation.surface: Planning to dine al fresco in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To destine something is to set it apart for a purpose, to plan it.

clue.text: Catch badly missed? Not half, he got a run!

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word missed is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder drops a catch, letting the batsman score a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps half of MISSED, the first three letters MIS. 'got' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to hear correctly is to catch someone's words badly.

clue.text: Remarkable occurrence left America almost in chaos

indicators.note: in chaos says the letters are thrown into disorder
almost drops the final letter of the word America

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a nearly ruined America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims AMERICA to AMERIC; with L, 'in chaos' rearranges LAMERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is an extraordinary, seemingly supernatural event.

clue.text: Love needed in order to be a musician

indicators.note: in places the letter for love within the order's letters

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire
love is nil in tennis, a zero, O

explanation.surface: Love is needed in order to become an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the tennis score zero, O. 'needed' and 'to be' are links; the instrument names the person who plays it, as players are named in orchestras.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestral player may be called by their instrument, so this woodwind instrument stands for its player.

clue.text: Treatment beginning for registered drug addict

parts.note: the use of something is how it is treated or handled

indicators.note: beginning for says to take the opening letter of the word registered

explanation.surface: A registered addict gets the start of treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes illegal drugs is a drug taker, so an addict is a habitual one.

clue.text: Admit a novice of less than average height

parts.note: L is for learner, a novice driver
something low is short, below average height

explanation.surface: Letting in a short beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novice' is L, from the learner plates on a British car.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to grant or concede it.

clue.text: A spike set up for a climber

indicators.note: set up in a down clue says the letters are written upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a nail is a metal spike

explanation.surface: A climbing spike is fixed in place for a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a piton and a mountaineer; the climber is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine that climbs up trees in tropical forests.

clue.text: Rise and fall of the Holy Roman Emperor

indicators.note: rise and fall says the down entry reads the same going up as coming down

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: The story of an emperor's rise and decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Several Holy Roman Emperors were named Otto, starting with Otto the Great.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto I founded the Holy Roman Empire in 962, and several of his successors bore his name.

clue.text: Cook in pan

explanation.surface: Prepare food in a frying pan.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook in an oven is one sense; to criticise severely, as a critic pans a show, is the other.

clue.text: Strange instances happening repeatedly

indicators.note: strange tells us the word instances is made into an odd new arrangement

explanation.surface: Odd cases that keep on recurring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unceasing goes on continually without a break.

clue.text: Perfect interpretation of Bach opera, gripping throughout

indicators.note: gripping says the rearranged letters hold the word for throughout within them
an interpretation of the words Bach opera renders them in a fresh order

parts.note: over means throughout, as in all over the world

explanation.surface: A flawless performance of an opera by Bach, enthralling from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts OVER inside ABREPROACH, an anagram of BACH OPERA, splitting it after AB. Bach never wrote an opera, which adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond criticism is blameless, flawless in conduct.
